blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the real roots of the following functions correct to two decimal places using the graphical method, by finding some interval of sign change: \(f(x) = x^{3} - x - 1\).
blocks.explanation:
This time no interval is given, so we first find one ourselves by trying whole numbers.
Then we draw \(y = x^3 - x - 1\) inside it and read the root to two decimal places.
Plan: continuity, scan whole numbers for a sign change, table at 0.1 steps, graph, zoom, LRT check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^3 - x - 1\).
To find: its real root, correct to two decimal places.
Method: the graphical method; step 1 of the method (find an interval of sign change) is needed because no interval is given.

Continuity
\[f(c) = \lim_{x \to c}(x^3 - x - 1) \quad \forall c \in \mathbb{R}\]
Why: \(f\) is a polynomial, so it is continuous for every real \(x\).

Find an interval of sign change
\[f(0) = -1,\quad f(1) = -1\]
\[f(2) = 8 - 2 - 1 = 5\]
\[f(1)\,f(2) = (-1)(5) < 0\]
Why: trying whole numbers, the sign first changes between 1 and 2, so \([1, 2]\) is an interval of sign change. Also \(f(-1) = -1\) and \(f(-2) = -7\): there is no sign change for negative \(x\) (this cubic has only one real root).

Draw the graph
Why: plot the points and join them smoothly (see the answer figure). The curve rises from \((1, -1)\) to \((2, 5)\) and crosses the axis between 1.3 and 1.4, close to 1.3.

Zoom in at steps of 0.01
\[f(1.30) = -0.1030\]
\[f(1.31) = -0.0619\]
\[f(1.32) = -0.0200\]
\[f(1.33) = 0.0226\]
\[f(1.34) = 0.0661\]
Why: the sign changes between 1.32 and 1.33. \(f(1.32) = -0.0200\) and \(f(1.33) = 0.0226\) are almost equal in size, so the crossing is near the middle; a closer look is needed to decide.

Check: confirm the two decimal places
\[f(1.315) = -0.0411 < 0\]
\[f(1.325) = 0.0012 > 0\]
Why: \(f(1.325)\) is already positive, so the root lies in \(]1.315, 1.325[\), and every number there rounds to 1.32. So \(x \approx 1.32\), as in the answer key.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = x^3 - x - 1 plotted through the points at steps of 0.1 on [1, 2]; the curve crosses the x-axis at about x = 1.32.
answer_figure.caption: Graph of \(y = x^{3} - x - 1\) on \([1, 2]\); it crosses the x-axis at \(x \approx 1.32\) (original drawing)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the answer key (Answers 8.1) the answers of Question 2 are printed straight after those of Question 1 without the label "2.": "1. (i) 0.36 (ii) 1.86 (i) 1.32 (ii) 0.85 (iii) 7.39". The second group (i) 1.32, (ii) 0.85, (iii) 7.39 belongs to Question 2. The answers themselves are correct.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the real roots of the following functions correct to two decimal places using the graphical method, by finding some interval of sign change: \(f(x) = xe^{x} - 2\).
blocks.explanation:
No interval is given, so we first find one from whole numbers.
Then we read where \(y = xe^{x} - 2\) crosses the \(x\)-axis, to two decimal places.
Plan: continuity, find the interval, table at 0.1 steps, graph, zoom, LRT check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = xe^{x} - 2\).
To find: its real root, correct to two decimal places.
Method: the graphical method; \(x\) appears both outside and inside the exponential, so the equation \(xe^{x} = 2\) cannot be solved by algebra.

Continuity
\[f(c) = \lim_{x \to c}(xe^{x} - 2) \quad \forall c \in \mathbb{R}\]
Why: \(x\) and \(e^{x}\) are continuous, so their product, and the product minus 2, is continuous everywhere.

Find an interval of sign change
\[f(0) = 0 - 2 = -2 < 0\]
\[f(1) = e - 2 = 0.7183 > 0\]
Why: the sign changes between 0 and 1, so \([0, 1]\) is an interval of sign change. For \(x < 0\), \(xe^{x}\) is negative, so \(f(x) < -2\): there is no root on the negative side.

Draw the graph
Why: plot the points and join them smoothly (see the answer figure). The curve rises from \((0, -2)\) to \((1, 0.72)\) and crosses the axis between 0.8 and 0.9, near the middle.

Check: confirm the two decimal places
\[f(0.845) = -0.0329 < 0\]
\[f(0.855) = 0.0104 > 0\]
Why: by the LRT the root lies in \(]0.845, 0.855[\), which rounds to 0.85, as in the answer key.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = x e^x - 2 plotted through the points at steps of 0.1 on [0, 1]; the curve crosses the x-axis at about x = 0.85.
answer_figure.caption: Graph of \(y = xe^{x} - 2\) on \([0, 1]\); it crosses the x-axis at \(x \approx 0.85\) (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find the real roots of the following functions correct to two decimal places using the graphical method, by finding some interval of sign change: \(f(x) = \ln(x) - 2\).
blocks.explanation:
No interval is given; \(\ln x\) grows slowly, so we must go up to fairly large whole numbers to see a sign change.
Then we read the root from the graph to two decimal places.
Plan: domain and continuity, find the interval, table, graph, zoom (keeping 5 decimals), LRT check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \ln(x) - 2\).
To find: its real root, correct to two decimal places.
Method: the graphical method, as the question asks. (This one can also be solved exactly, which we use as a check at the end.)

Domain and continuity
\[f(c) = \lim_{x \to c}(\ln x - 2) \quad \forall c > 0\]
Why: \(\ln x\) is defined and continuous only for \(x > 0\), so we search only among positive \(x\).

Find an interval of sign change
\[f(1) = 0 - 2 = -2\]
\[f(7) = 1.9459 - 2 = -0.0541\]
\[f(8) = 2.0794 - 2 = 0.0794\]
Why: \(f(1), f(2), \ldots, f(7)\) are all negative; the first sign change is between 7 and 8, so \([7, 8]\) is an interval of sign change. \(\ln x\) is increasing, so there is only one root.

Draw the graph
Why: on \([7, 8]\) the values are very small, so use a large \(y\)-scale (steps of 0.02). The curve is almost a straight line from \((7, -0.054)\) to \((8, 0.079)\) and crosses the axis between 7.3 and 7.4 (see the answer figure).

Zoom in at steps of 0.01 (5 decimal places)
\[f(7.37) = -0.00258\]
\[f(7.38) = -0.00123\]
\[f(7.39) = 0.00013\]
\[f(7.40) = 0.00148\]
\[f(7.41) = 0.00283\]
Why: \(f\) changes very slowly here, so 4 decimals are not enough to see the signs clearly. The sign changes between 7.38 and 7.39, and \(f(7.39) = 0.00013\) is almost 0, so \(x \approx 7.39\).

Check: confirm the two decimal places
\[f(7.385) = -0.00055 < 0\]
\[f(7.395) = 0.00080 > 0\]
Why: by the LRT the root lies in \(]7.385, 7.395[\), which rounds to 7.39. Exactly: \(\ln x = 2 \Rightarrow x = e^{2} = 7.3891\), which also rounds to 7.39, as in the answer key.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = ln x - 2 plotted through the points at steps of 0.1 on [7, 8]; the curve crosses the x-axis at about x = 7.39.
answer_figure.caption: Graph of \(y = \ln x - 2\) on \([7, 8]\); it crosses the x-axis at \(x \approx 7.39\) (original drawing)
